chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: United States Capitol Police
paragraphs: (a) There is established in the legislative branch the United States Capitol Police, which shall serve as the law enforcement and protective service of the Congress of the United States and shall be charged with protecting the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, Members of Congress, officers of Congress, congressional employees, witnesses, invited guests, visitors, congressional proceedings, and the functions of the legislative branch.

(b) Officers of the Capitol Police shall be sworn federal law enforcement officers. While engaged in the performance of official duties, officers of the Capitol Police may carry firearms, make arrests without warrant for any offense against the United States committed in their presence, make arrests for any felony cognizable under the laws of the United States if the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the person to be arrested has committed or is committing such felony, execute and serve warrants, subpoenas, summonses, and other lawful process issued under the authority of the United States or either House of Congress, and exercise such other law enforcement powers as are necessary to carry out this Act.

(c) Before exercising law enforcement authority, each officer of the Capitol Police shall take an oath to support and defend the Constitution of the United States and to faithfully discharge the duties of office.

(d) The Chief shall prescribe qualifications, training requirements, standards of conduct, equipment rules, identification requirements, and procedures for commissioning officers of the Capitol Police.

(e) Civilian employees, administrative employees, analysts, dispatchers, technicians, security support personnel, and other employees of the Capitol Police shall not exercise sworn law enforcement authority unless appointed, qualified, and commissioned as officers under this Act.

(f) The Capitol Police shall operate under the direction and oversight of the Capitol Police Board, subject to the separate constitutional authority of each House over its own chamber, proceedings, rules, officers, privileges, discipline, and controlled spaces.

(g) The Capitol Police may preserve order, protect persons and property, prevent obstruction of congressional business, enforce applicable laws, enforce lawful security orders, regulate access as authorized by law or congressional rule, and make arrests for violations of law committed within its jurisdiction.

(h) The Capitol Police shall act in aid of Congress and shall not exercise independent legislative, judicial, disciplinary, or political authority. Nothing in this Act shall be construed to authorize the Capitol Police to decide questions of order, punish Members, determine privileges of either House, suspend proceedings, control recognition, prevent lawful votes, interfere with debate, or alter the internal rules of either House.

(i) In matters concerning chamber access, chamber proceedings, decorum, removal of disorderly persons, enforcement of House or Senate rules, or protection of the privileges of either House, the Capitol Police shall act subject to the lawful direction of the Speaker, President pro tempore, Presiding Officer, or Sergeant at Arms of the relevant House.

(j) The Capitol Police shall enforce law, security regulations, access rules, and lawful orders in a neutral manner. No officer, employee, policy, regulation, deployment, arrest, removal, investigation, protective action, or security measure may be used for the purpose of favoring or disfavoring any political party, faction, Member, officer, witness, nominee, ideology, or viewpoint.

(k) The Capitol Police may coordinate with the Sergeant at Arms of either House, the Chief of the Capitol Police, the Capitol Police Board, and other lawful authorities as necessary to protect Congress, but no outside authority may supersede the control of either House over its own proceedings, chamber, rules, and privileges.

sections.heading: Capitol Police Board
paragraphs: (a) There is established a Capitol Police Board, which shall exercise general direction, oversight, and administrative control over the United States Capitol Police, subject to the authority of each House over its own proceedings, chamber, officers, rules, privileges, and controlled spaces.

(b) The Board shall consist of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President pro tempore of the Senate, the Majority Leader of the House of Representatives, the Majority Leader of the Senate, the Sergeant at Arms of the House of Representatives, and the Sergeant at Arms of the Senate.
(c) Each member of the Board shall have one vote. Except as otherwise provided by this Act, any action of the Board shall require the affirmative vote of a majority of the members then serving.

(d) The Board shall select a Chair from among its members at the beginning of each Congress and whenever a vacancy in the chair occurs. If the Board is unable to select a Chair, the Speaker and the President pro tempore shall jointly designate a Chair. If the Speaker and the President pro tempore are unable to agree, the chairmanship shall rotate monthly between the Sergeant at Arms of the House of Representatives and the Sergeant at Arms of the Senate until the Board selects a Chair.

(e) The Board may meet upon the call of the Chair, the Speaker, the President pro tempore, or any three members of the Board. The Board may meet in regular session, special session, emergency session, or closed session when necessary to consider sensitive security information, personnel matters, classified information, threats to Congress, or matters involving the safety of Members, officers, employees, witnesses, or visitors.

(f) The Board shall supervise the Chief of the Capitol Police, approve major policies of the Capitol Police, review security operations, issue regulations necessary to carry out this Act, receive reports required by this Act, inspect records, review disciplinary matters, order corrective action, and ensure coordination between the Capitol Police and the officers of both Houses.

(g) The Board may approve, amend, suspend, or disapprove any regulation, policy, directive, general order, training standard, access rule, disciplinary rule, use-of-force policy, interagency agreement, deployment policy, or emergency procedure issued by the Chief.

(h) The Chief may issue regulations, general orders, directives, and procedures governing access to the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, security operations, officer conduct, emergency response, interagency coordination, protective assignments, arrests, removals, detentions, use of force, records, discipline, training, deployment outside jurisdiction, and any other operational matter necessary to carry out this Act.

(i) A regulation, general order, directive, or procedure issued by the Chief shall remain subject to review by the Board. The Board may require prior approval for any category of regulation or action that substantially affects the authority, jurisdiction, command, discipline, training, public access rules, use of force, outside deployments, interagency coordination, or operations of the Capitol Police.

(j) No regulation, order, policy, or directive of the Board may override the Constitution, an Act of Congress, the rules of either House, an order of either House, or the lawful authority of the Speaker, the President pro tempore, the Presiding Officer of either House, or the Sergeant at Arms of either House over that House’s proceedings, chamber, officers, privileges, discipline, or controlled spaces.

(k) The Board may require the Chief, Deputy Chief, or any officer or employee of the Capitol Police to provide reports, testimony, records, explanations, or other information concerning the operations, conduct, policies, discipline, expenditures, or security actions of the Capitol Police.

(l) The Board may review any major security incident, emergency response, lockdown, evacuation, arrest of a Member of Congress, use of force resulting in injury, death, or detention, deployment outside jurisdiction, complaint of misconduct, or alleged violation of this Act. (m)The Board may direct the Chief to adopt, amend, suspend, or repeal any policy, practice, regulation, training requirement, disciplinary measure, access rule, or operational procedure of the Capitol Police where the Board determines that such action is necessary to protect Congress, ensure accountability, preserve order, correct misconduct, or carry out this Act.

(n) The Board may delegate routine administrative and operational duties to the Chief, but no delegation shall be construed to transfer final oversight authority from the Board or to prevent the Board from reviewing, modifying, suspending, or reversing an action of the Chief.

(o) The Board may not use its authority to favor or disfavor any political party, faction, Member of Congress, officer of Congress, witness, nominee, employee, ideology, viewpoint, or lawful legislative position.

(p) The Board shall maintain records of its votes, regulations, formal directives, emergency approvals, disciplinary review actions, and other official actions taken under this Act. Records concerning classified information, sensitive security information, personnel discipline, or active threats may be maintained in closed form, but shall remain available for lawful review by the Board and by any committee or officer authorized by either House.

(q) The Board shall submit a report to the House of Representatives and the Senate to be read during session, at least once during each Congress concerning the administration, operations, discipline, training, complaints, use of force, arrests, removals, protective services, emergency actions, and major security incidents of the Capitol Police, except that classified information, sensitive security information, and personally identifying security information may be submitted in a closed session if necessary.
